chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from his narrators, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'That is a Day for which the people will gather, and that is a Day that is (to be) witnessed.' He said: That which is the witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and that for which people will gather is the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the 'Day of Gathering' and the 'Day of Witnessing' in Quran 11:103?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) distinction between the eschatological gathering of humanity on the Day of Resurrection and the specific witnessing of the Day of Arafah, highlighting the latter's unique status in Shia exegesis. This interpretation underscores the theological significance of Arafah not merely as a ritual site but as a day of divine observation and mercy, linking the Hajj pilgrimage directly to the ultimate accountability of the Hereafter.
